title: Finite centre-phase fanout across two shared-source panels
body:
## Result

This package gives an exact local interface construction for two invocations of the selected #1094 centre phase when they share the same eight source-row values and have disjoint dirty target panels. The eight rank-8 centre maps are evaluated once and their outputs are scattered to both panels. All 352 target updates are retained.

The complete two-call centre-phase invoice falls from 416 to 384 scalar actions: rank-8 moves 16→8, source copies 16→8 and centre clears 32→16, with the target updates unchanged. The exact 9-stage planning profile changes from eight to four rank-8 children per call. Under the repository's favorable relaxation this gives `a_cap≈0.003212972894`; the unchanged bit supplier then binds at `a=0.001733427039589844234749`, limiting a whole-bound gain to at most 3.4536%. This is a finite local construction and a screened cap, **not a new accepted κ**. The selected result is unchanged.

## Evidence and reproduction

The verifier pins the selected record, review, source manifest, certificate, and the 480-helper replay archive. It reconstructs all eight selected rank-8 events and their 22 target updates, then compares the fused and separate calls over all 1,601 source, target-dirt and private-centre basis coordinates plus a dense rational fixture. It verifies three negative controls for a changed source, omitted target update and missing clear.

```sh
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/centre-fanout-two-panel-seed962302
```

The registered replay passes with `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE ... outcome=completed`. Exact evidence and source pins are in `research/centre-fanout-two-panel-seed962302/`.

## Scope and remaining work

The construction assumes identical values on the eight source rows and disjoint target panels. It does not establish that eligible invocation pairs occur in the selected supplier schedule, or charge any source preparation, owner, precision, hosting or composition cost needed to realize them. The unchanged bit supplier binds in the optimistic screen, so no selected κ follows from this result.

The scope and outcome are recorded in [Discussion #1516](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1516#discussioncomment-18918111). This is distinct from PR #1704's bit-side pair-sum scatter construction and PR #1703's one-touch rank-2 retiming obstruction.

Predecessor: Rohan Arun's selected PR #1094 and retained gauge44-slots-t16 provider lineage. Prepared by Cinna Davis with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in scoping, cost analysis, exact verifier implementation and exposition. No human or Lean proof is claimed.
